pr_title: apiextensions: validate list-type map+set uniqueness in CRs
pr_body:
/kind api-change
/kind bug

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/84724.

```release-note
Fixed missing validation of uniqueness of list items in lists with `x-kubernetes-list-type: map` or x-kubernetes-list-type: set` in CustomResources.
```

Hello @liggitt, @sttts 
Bug Triage team here for the 1.18 release. This is a friendly reminder that code freeze is scheduled for 5 March. Is this PR appears to be blocking https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/84724, is this still intended for milestone 1.18?
@apelisse addressed your comments.

I have a couple of additional comments. 

I'm really not convinced that we want `listMapKeys` fields to be anything but required. Having a "nil" item validate because both keys are missing and transforming this into a valid case really feels wrong. As far as I know, we have one such case in Kubernetes, that's the protocol in the list of ports of the podspec. We might find a way to fix that one specifically, but I'd rather not generalize this problem. Alternatively, we could allow these to be if they have a default value, and in this case consider the default as the key value. IOW, "required or has a default" (that would also work for the protocol problem).

Second, I was discussion ratcheting with Daniel, and forcing the created objects to pass this validation only works if we assume that no controller/system is currently creating invalid objects. This change would break such a controller?

> I'm really not convinced that we want listMapKeys fields to be anything but required. Having a "nil" item validate because both keys are missing and transforming this into a valid case really feels wrong. As far as I know, we have one such case in Kubernetes, that's the protocol in the list of ports of the podspec. We might find a way to fix that one specifically, but I'd rather not generalize this problem. Alternatively, we could allow these to be if they have a default value, and in this case consider the default as the key value. IOW, "required or has a default" (that would also work for the protocol problem).

All this is done via ratcheting validation, i.e. we enforce required or a default. We forbid nullable: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88076. Please review.

> Second, I was discussion ratcheting with Daniel, and forcing the created objects to pass this validation only works if we assume that no controller/system is currently creating invalid objects. This change would break such a controller?

This is what we always do in those cases, ratcheting validation. It is the very reason why this issue is marked urgent for months. The more we wait (1.18 is around the corner) the more controllers will exist. I bet the number is zero today.

Anyone defining a CRD that uses list-type: map/set must be able to rely on the documented semantics (we rely on them ourselves in server-side-apply). It is very important we not allow data that violates those semantics, and do so as soon as possible.

> Alternatively, we could allow these to be if they have a default value, and in this case consider the default as the key value. IOW, "required or has a default" (that would also work for the protocol problem).

That's what we settled on. Disallowing nullable and making the key attributes either be required or defaulted gives this set validation reasonable inputs to work with, and allows evolution or recovery from underspecified key sets (e.g. an underspecified item schema for a port realizes in the future it needs a protocol field that should be added to the item key specification, and needs to provide a default for existing persisted data that lacked that field).

/lgtm
/approve

issue_context.title: list-type set and map lack CR validation
issue_context.body:
In 1.16 we added `x-kubernetes-list-type` fields for CRDs. Lists of type map and set have uniqueness invariants on keys (map) and whole elements (set). These invariants must be checked during create and update validation in the CR registry.

To be backported to 1.16.
comments:
SSA equality for merging of sets and maps must match the equality used in the CR validation.

If SSA uses semantic equality for CRDs, this is probably a blocker for SSA GA until we have a normalization story implemented for CRDs (which replaces the need of semantic equality in post-decode logic).

/cc @lavalamp @deads2k

> SSA equality for merging of sets and maps must match the equality used in the CR validation.

> If SSA uses semantic equality for CRDs, this is probably a blocker for SSA GA until we have a normalization story implemented for CRDs (which replaces the need of semantic equality in post-decode logic).

SSA uses `reflect.DeepEqual` (actually, our own implementation of it) for built-in types and CRs. But it's also looking through `built-in -> unstructured` (normalization for built-in objects), which means that we're fine doing that. The biggest problem I see is that we deserialize the applied object directly into an unstructured, which means there is no normalization for that, that might be a problem.

I think comparison happens on fields that have been selected first with a field set, I'm not sure if that is neutral or helps with this problem.

It (SSA) does verify key-uniqueness.

I took pains to make it preserve list order but I think the json/yaml parser defeats this at the moment :/

Anyway, the result of SSA being overly / underly picky about differences isn't too bad: it means users get more or fewer conflicts. API designers shouldn't be using the things that will trigger the edge cases to drive behavioral differences anyway, as SSA already doesn't make it easy (or possible) to "own" the difference between e.g. unset / nil.

So, I'm not sure this is actually a blocker, the consequence isn't severe and well-written CRDs shouldn't have the problem anyway?

Without even considering CRs, we have a problem because of how we decode existing objects and apply objects differently. Possibly, a field can be set to null in apply and be `omitEmpty`'d in etcd and they'll look different to us, impacting `sets` of atomic?

Stefan and Jordan talked about this on slack, here's what we agree on:
1. Validation ratcheting is less risky than allowing known-bad data to continue being persisted in new CR objects
2. We would like the patch to be back-portable to 1.16,
3. We would like the validation to run even if server-side apply is disabled (mostly because we can't enable it everywhere just now, and it goes again 2. anyway)

> Validation ratcheting is more risky than adding validation to existing objects to verify that the listType properties are respected

We were saying ratcheting validation was *less* risky than allowing known-bad data to continue being persisted in new CR objects.

> We would like the validation to run even if server-side apply is disabled (mostly because we can't enable it everywhere just now, and it goes again 2. anyway)

The list-type semantics are not documented to only apply to server-side apply, and are useful for describing the data structure behavior of the custom resource. I agree we should enforce the semantics of the documented API regardless of SSA enablement/use.

We might be able to run it everywhere now if we don't persist the field,
have we tried?

review_comments: should we check that k is scalar and error early if not?
Don't we check that in the schema already that the field types are scalar? Then we should never get here, although this code will even work if they are not scalar.

I would have guessed a null item was treated like an empty map for key-computation purposes? e.g. the key of `null` is `{}` and the key of {} is `{}`. I wouldn't expect to be allowed to have `null` and `{}` both present in a map-list.
If that turns out to be the case, make sure there's a unit test for this

adding a `map[string]interface{}{}` here would let us use the index as-is in case of a duplicate

could share a single empty map between all nil items to avoid useless allocations
I implemented strict comparison now. Should we unify enpty and null? We have to decided => Slack.
for `list-type: set`, we compare list items strictly (`null != {} != [] != ""`). this would be another candidate for a normalization pass that would normalize {} and [] to null prior to comparison.
Updated the algorithm for maps (sets is unchanged), and also added test cases for single-key and multi-key cases with nil items, nil fields and undefined fields.
